researched_by: the operator's own destination websites (elan-valley.co.uk, llandegfedd.co.uk, llys-y-fran.co.uk), the Elan Valley Trust's own pages, the Bannau Brycheiniog reservoir passport booklet, and van-user site listings; no company-wide overnight policy document exists to read
policy_summary:
The fifth water company in the dataset, and the one that shows the landowner tier has no single model at all. Northumbrian sells the night at seven reservoirs on one booking system. Yorkshire Water refuses it in a sentence and leaves the gates open. Severn Trent refuses it and locks the gates. South West Water bans it outright and runs campsites through a charity. WELSH WATER SELLS YOU THE DAY - at three commercialised destinations, with a published tariff that names motorhomes - AND SELLS YOU A PITCH AT ONE OF THEM. There is no company-wide overnight scheme, no aire, no reservoir stopover network, and no published statement anywhere on the estate about sleeping in a vehicle, for or against.

The estate splits cleanly in two. First, three heavily invested visitor destinations, each with its own separate domain and its own tariff: Elan Valley (elan-valley.co.uk), Llandegfedd (llandegfedd.co.uk) and Llys-y-Frân (llys-y-fran.co.uk). These are run as attractions - visitor centre, cafe, watersports, pay and display - and the water company's parking income is the point. Second, everything else: Talybont, Pontsticill, Llyn Brianne, Usk, Cantref, Llwyn-on and the rest, which have free or informal car parks, no staff after dark, and nothing published at all.

The single most important finding is the one the parking pages do not mention. LLYS-Y-FRÂN HAS A WELSH WATER CAMPSITE. It is not on any parking page, it is not called an aire, and it is reachable only from the /camping-west-wales/ page under the destination site. Hardstanding pitches with and without electric hook-up, grass pitches likewise, 8x8 metre plots, six people, GBP 23 to GBP 45 a night depending on pitch and season, opening 27 March, a chemical toilet disposal point, heated showers, cafe, shop and free wi-fi - and booking exclusively through Pitch-Up. A water company running a graded touring park is exactly the category the method doc warns about: council and landowner campsites live in a different department from parking and never link to each other.

The second finding worth the file on its own is at Elan Valley: a landowner tariff that names motorhomes explicitly and charges them DOUBLE. GBP 3.00 for one hour against GBP 1.50 for a car, GBP 10.00 for over three hours against GBP 6.00, and a GBP 60.00 annual pass against GBP 40.00. This is a large vehicle surcharge, not a prohibition - Welsh Water is happy to take a motorhome's money by the hour and says nothing at all about the night. Note that it is the WATER COMPANY that sets this tariff, not the Trust that holds the estate (see notes).

The hardest restriction on the estate is at Llandegfedd, and it is mechanical rather than legal. Site access is 09:00-17:00 from 1 March to 31 October and 09:00-16:00 in winter, parking is GBP 3.00 a day with the first hour free, the North car park runs 09:00-17:00 in season only, and the visitor guidance is explicit: 'Please ensure vehicles are removed from the car parks by the advertised times as gates are locked overnight.' A locked gate ends the argument in a way that no sign does.

Direction of travel: monetisation of the three destinations, indifference everywhere else. Llys-y-Frân took GBP 4m of Welsh Water investment plus GBP 1.7m of ERDF money through Welsh Government and has gone from a reservoir with a car park to a graded holiday park in under a decade. Elan Valley has an annual pass and an EV charger. Nothing comparable is happening at Talybont or Llyn Brianne, and nothing is likely to until somebody complains.
notes:
ESTABLISH THE ELAN VALLEY RELATIONSHIP BEFORE YOU RECORD ANYTHING THERE. The Elan Estate is owned by Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water, but the greater part of it is vested in the ELAN VALLEY TRUST on a 999-YEAR LEASE. The Trust was established by Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water, by agreement with Government, in 1989 - it was formerly the Welsh Water Elan Trust - and is registered charity number 1001347. It administers the 72 square mile estate as landlord to 28 farms and 38 houses, manages in excess of 7,000 acres of farmland, and employs the countryside ranger team. So: freehold Welsh Water, working control Elan Valley Trust, on a lease that outlasts everyone.

The split that matters on the ground is that the VISITOR CENTRE IS THE EXCEPTION. elanvalley.org.uk states the Visitor Centre is 'operated by Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water', the tariff is published on Welsh Water's own elan-valley.co.uk, and the contact numbers are split accordingly - Visitor Centre matters to Welsh Water on 01597 810880, estate and property matters to the Elan Valley Trust on 01597 810449. Treat the Visitor Centre car park as Welsh Water's and the rest of the estate's car parks as the Trust's, and say so in any record.

THERE ARE TWO ELAN VALLEY WEBSITES AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT BODIES. elanvalley.org.uk is the Trust. elan-valley.co.uk is Welsh Water. They cross-link, they share branding, and they answer the same questions differently. Anyone researching this valley who does not notice will attribute the Trust's estate rules to the water company or vice versa. The same hazard as the Bannau Brycheiniog rebrand, for the same reason: one place, two publishers.

NO CAMPING IN THE ELAN VALLEY IS WELSH WATER'S OR THE TRUST'S. The Trust runs self-catering cottages and nothing else. Elan Oaks Camping and Caravan Site, the Elan Valley Hotel and the 5-star Elan Valley Lodge are all separate businesses listed as third-party accommodation - name them as private supply so nobody researches them under this authority. Likewise at Llys-y-Frân there are TWO campsites with confusingly similar names: Llys-y-Frân Lakeview Campsite is Welsh Water's and is recorded here; Llys-y-Frân Meadow Campsite (llysyfranmeadow.co.uk) is a private neighbour and is not.

THE OWNERSHIP TANGLE AT TALYBONT AND PONTSTICILL is the reason these records exist here rather than in bannau-brycheiniog-national-park.json. That file deliberately did not record them, correctly identifying the reservoirs as Welsh Water's. But the car parks around them are a patchwork: Neuadd car park at Talybont-on-Usk is Natural Resources Wales, the Blaen y Glyn and Taf Fechan forest car parks are NRW, and NRW's position is flatly that 'overnight parking is not allowed at any NRW site'. Do not assume a car park beside a Welsh Water reservoir is Welsh Water's - in Bannau Brycheiniog the odds are against it. The two records here are held at low confidence for exactly that reason.

WELSH WATER DOES MAKE BYELAWS, BUT NOT ABOUT PARKING. Llyn Brianne has been governed since 19 April 2011 by the 'Dwr Cymru Cyf, Llyn Brianne Bylaws 2010', which prohibit bathing, diving, swimming, any boat including kayaks and canoes, and angling without a Welsh Water permit. They regulate the WATER. No equivalent instrument covering car parks, camping or overnight vehicles was found anywhere on the estate, which means the position on land is a landowner's rule enforceable only by asking someone to leave - not an offence.

The research lesson for the rest of the landowner tier: do not generalise from any one water company. Five are now done and all five differ - Northumbrian sells the night, Yorkshire refuses it on a webpage, Severn Trent refuses it with a padlock, South West Water bans it and runs campsites through a charity, Welsh Water prices the day and sells pitches. The tell is the web estate. A company with separate branded destination domains is running attractions and will price the day; a company with one booking system across many reservoirs is running a stopover network and will price the night; a company with a single corporate FAQ has thought about it once and said no.
open_questions: Is the Elan Valley Visitor Centre car park gated or locked overnight? The tariff and the visitor centre hours (09:00-17:00 April to October, 10:00-16:00 October to March) are published; no closing time for the car park itself is. This is the single biggest gap in the file.

Does Welsh Water publish an overnight parking rule ANYWHERE? Nothing was found on any of the three destination sites or the corporate site. Absence of a published rule is the finding, but a signed rule on the ground would not appear online.
Was 2026 the FIRST season of the Llys-y-Frân campsite, or is 27 March 2026 simply this year's season opening? The camping page gives the date without saying which.
Is there a maximum stay at Llys-y-Frân, and does it accept large motorhomes on the hardstandings? Plots are stated as 8x8 metres, which is tight for an 8m van plus awning space.
Who actually owns the car parks at Talybont Reservoir and Pontsticill Reservoir - Welsh Water, NRW, or the Bannau Brycheiniog National Park Authority? Only the water is confirmed as Welsh Water's.
Is there a car park at the Llyn Brianne dam and who owns it? Van users list the dam as a stop; no coordinate or ownership could be corroborated, so no pin is recorded.

What are the Elan Valley Trust's charges and rules at the estate car parks away from the Visitor Centre - Garreg-ddu, Pen y Garreg, Craig Goch and Claerwen? The Trust's directions and parking page could not be loaded in this session.

Do the other water companies operating in Wales and the border (Severn Trent, Hafren Dyfrdwy, United Utilities in the Dee catchment) run anything comparable? That decides whether the landowner-water tier is three files or twelve.

sites.name: Llys-y-Frân Lakeview Campsite
sites.price_note: By pitch type and season: hardstanding with electric hook-up GBP 35-45, hardstanding without GBP 28-33, grass with electric GBP 30-40, grass without GBP 23-33. Motorhomes and campervans take the hardstandings.
facilities: heated shower block with family changing
free wi-fi in the visitor centre
sites.search_hint: Llys-y-Fran Lakeview Campsite, Clarbeston Road, Pembrokeshire
sites.notes: THIS IS THE RECORD THE PARKING PAGES DO NOT MENTION. Welsh Water owns and operates a graded touring campsite on its own reservoir site, reachable only from the camping section of the destination website - there is no link from the parking tariff page and no link back. Pitches are 8x8 metres for up to six people, in four grades: hardstanding with and without electric hook-up, grass with and without. Season opening given as 27 March 2026. Booking is EXCLUSIVELY through Pitch-Up - you cannot turn up and pay at the gate, which makes this provision you must plan for rather than provision you can use. The chemical toilet disposal point is the detail that matters to a van: it is the only confirmed chemical disposal on the whole Welsh Water estate. Site telephone 01437 532273, llysyfran@dwrcymru.com. The wider site took GBP 4m of Welsh Water investment plus GBP 1.7m of European Regional Development Fund money through Welsh Government. NOT to be confused with Llys-y-Frân Meadow Campsite, which is a private neighbouring business.
sites.geocode_precision: the Llys-y-Frân visitor centre and lake site, on the operator's own sat-nav postcode SA63 4RR; the campsite is on this site overlooking the lake

sites.name: Llandegfedd Lake
sites.search_hint: Llandegfedd Reservoir visitor centre, Coed y Paen, Pontypool
sites.notes: The hardest restriction on the Welsh Water estate, and it is a padlock rather than a rule. Site access is 09:00-17:00 from 1 March to 31 October and 09:00-16:00 from 1 November, and the visitor guidance says in terms: 'Please ensure vehicles are removed from the car parks by the advertised times as gates are locked overnight.' The North car park opens 1 March to 31 October, 09:00-17:00 only. Parking is GBP 3.00 a day with the first hour free. Closes 14:00 on 24 December and shut on 25, 26 and 31 December. Independently listed by van users as daytime-only parking suitable for motorhomes. There is nothing here about sleeping specifically - the gate simply removes the option, which is why applies_to is all_vehicles rather than adapted_for_sleeping. Visitor centre, Lakeside Cafe, activity centre with hot showers, and a watersports programme March to October.
sites.geocode_precision: the visitor centre and main top car park above the reservoir at Coed y Paen

sites.search_hint: Elan Valley Visitor Centre, Rhayader, Powys
sites.notes: RECORDED AS A RESTRICTION BECAUSE OF THE TARIFF, NOT BECAUSE OF A NIGHT RULE - no overnight statement of any kind is published for this car park, and status is left unknown for that reason. What IS published, and is unusual enough to be the point of the record, is a landowner tariff that names motorhomes as a class and charges them exactly DOUBLE the car rate at every band, up to GBP 10.00 for over three hours and GBP 60.00 for an annual pass. That is a large-vehicle surcharge from a water company, and it is the first of its kind found in this dataset. Operated by Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water, NOT by the Elan Valley Trust which holds the rest of the estate - see the file notes. Visitor centre hours 09:00-17:00 April to October, 10:00-16:00 October to March, closed Christmas Day; whether the car park itself is gated with them is not published. Three miles west of Rhayader on the B4518.
sites.geocode_precision: the visitor centre car park below Caban-coch dam, on the operator's published sat-nav postcode LD6 5HP

sites.name: Talybont Reservoir
sites.notes: The reservoir is confirmed as Welsh Water's, and bannau-brycheiniog-national-park.json deliberately left it out of that file for that reason, which is why it sits here. The CAR PARK ownership is a different question and is not confirmed - Neuadd car park at the north end of the reservoir is Natural Resources Wales, and NRW's blanket position is that overnight parking is not allowed at any NRW site. Van-user listings record Talybont Reservoir as daytime-only parking suitable for motorhomes at LD3 7YS. No Welsh Water statement, no signage wording and no instrument could be found, so this record is inference from the listing plus the surrounding NRW regime and is held at low confidence. A single-track lane on the eastern shore, no facilities. Anyone verifying should establish first WHICH car park they are standing in.
sites.geocode_precision: LD3 7YS postcode point at the north end of the reservoir, the postcode the van-user listing gives for Talybont Reservoir; not a surveyed car park entrance

sites.name: Llys-y-Frân Lake day car park
sites.price_note: Pay and display, no motorhome tariff published: 1 hour GBP 1.50, 4 hours GBP 4.00, all day GBP 6.00 April to October and GBP 1.50 November to March, annual pass GBP 40.00. Free for Blue Badge holders in the disabled bays only.
sites.search_hint: Llys-y-Fran visitor centre car park, Clarbeston Road, Pembrokeshire
sites.notes: Deliberately unpinned: it shares a site with the campsite record above and giving it the same coordinate would put two records on one point. Recorded separately because the day car park and the campsite are different offers on the same land with different rules and different money. The site is stated as open all year and no overnight rule is published, but Welsh Water now sells pitches fifty metres away, so the day car park is plainly not the overnight offer. That is inference, hence low confidence and unknown status. Unlike Elan Valley there is NO separate motorhome tariff here.

sites.name: Elan Valley estate car parks (Elan Valley Trust)
sites.search_hint: Elan Valley Trust car parks Garreg-ddu Pen y Garreg Craig Goch Claerwen
sites.notes: PLACEHOLDER FOR AN UNRESOLVED OWNERSHIP QUESTION, not a researched rule. The dam car parks up the valley - Garreg-ddu and the Foel Tower, Pen y Garreg, Craig Goch and the long road to Claerwen - are on the part of the estate vested in the Elan Valley Trust on its 999-year lease, not on the Visitor Centre land Welsh Water operates directly. The Trust's own directions and parking page could not be loaded in this session, so no charge, no hours and no overnight position is recorded and no coordinates are given. Do not publish this record; do not assume the Visitor Centre tariff applies up the valley. Somebody needs to read elanvalley.org.uk/visit/directions-parking/ and split this into real records, possibly into a separate Elan Valley Trust file given the Trust is a distinct charity (1001347) with a 999-year interest.

sites.name: Pontsticill Reservoir
sites.search_hint: Pontsticill Reservoir, Merthyr Tydfil, Taf Fechan
sites.notes: Recorded because bannau-brycheiniog-national-park.json identifies Pontsticill as Welsh Water's and deliberately excluded it, so it belongs in this file. Beyond that almost nothing is established. The reservoir straddles Powys and Merthyr Tydfil county borough, is operated by Welsh Water, and the woodland on the western side is managed by Natural Resources Wales with the Taf Fechan Forest car parks belonging to NRW - which bans overnight parking at all its sites. The Brecon Mountain Railway also has parking of its own on the eastern side. No Welsh Water car park could be confirmed, no coordinate could be corroborated, so lat and lon are null. Pontsticill is one of the four reservoirs in the Bannau Brycheiniog / Welsh Water Reservoir Passport canoeing scheme, with Pentwyn, Usk and Beacons - that scheme requires a passport displayed in the vehicle windscreen, which is the only Welsh Water rule found anywhere that touches a parked vehicle.

sites.name: Llyn Brianne
sites.notes: Recorded for the INSTRUMENT rather than for a parking rule. Llyn Brianne has been governed since 19 April 2011 by the 'Dwr Cymru Cyf, Llyn Brianne Bylaws 2010' - the only Welsh Water byelaws found in this research. They prohibit bathing, diving and swimming, the use of any boat including kayaks, canoes and jet-skis, and angling without a Welsh Water permit. They are WATER byelaws: nothing in them was found to touch car parks, camping or sleeping in a vehicle, so a van at the dam at 2am is not committing a byelaw offence on the evidence available. The dam spillway is a well-known sight when the reservoir is spilling and van users list the dam as a stop, but no car park ownership and no coordinate could be corroborated from a second source, so lat and lon are deliberately null. The approach is a long single-track road from Rhandirmwyn or Llanwrtyd Wells; the reservoir sits on the Carmarthenshire / Powys boundary in the headwaters of the Towy.

sites.name: All other Welsh Water reservoirs and operational land
sites.notes: THE HONEST ESTATE-WIDE POSITION IS THAT THERE ISN'T ONE. Welsh Water publishes no company-wide overnight parking policy, no reservoir stopover scheme, no permit and no prohibition. Away from Elan Valley, Llandegfedd and Llys-y-Frân - Usk, Cantref, Beacons, Llwyn-on, Pentwyn, Cray, Crai, Alaw, Cefni, Llandegla and the rest - the position is simply unpublished. Practically that means a landowner's rule, enforceable by being asked to leave and nothing more, exactly as in the Bannau Brycheiniog analysis. This record exists so that the absence is on the register rather than being re-searched every year, and so that nobody assumes the Northumbrian Water pattern of a paid overnight scheme applies here. It does not.
